slides.title: The nurse in the pediatric clinic is caring for a 6-year-old client with recurre
text: Question: The nurse in the pediatric clinic is caring for a 6-year-old client with recurrent group A streptococcal pharyngitis and inflammation of the conjunctivae. The eyelids are edematous. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
A. Moisten a clean compress with warm water.
B. Remind the client to avoid rubbing their eyes.
C. Instill newly prescribed antibiotic drops in both eyes.
D. Wipe each client eye beginning at the inner canthus.
Correct answer: A. Moisten a clean compress with warm water.
notes: Crusted drainage must be softened and removed before medication can reach the eye, so the nurse first prepares a warm, moist compress. Then wipe from the inner to the outer canthus with a clean area of cloth for each eye, instill drops, and teach not to rub the eyes.
(Answer key not on the slide; worked out with NCLEX reasoning, so check it against your class notes.)
